transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This sounds like an earth-leakage fault, which is common with induction hobs when internal components degrade. Because this trips your main electrics, it is potentially dangerous and you should stop using the hob until it is checked by a qualified engineer. To help narrow down whether the issue is inside the hob or in the wiring, please check: Is your hob hard-wired into a fused spur (a small switch box on the wall) or plugged into a socket?
There's a cooker switch on the wall, but I don't know about the fuse box side of it. Also I did notice a faint electrical smell once after it tripped. Should I just leave it off then?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, please leave it switched off and do not use it again. The combination of tripping the electrics and a faint electrical smell suggests an internal earth-leakage fault in the induction electronics or wiring. This is a safety hazard that cannot be fixed by resetting switches; it requires a qualified engineer to isolate and repair the faulty component safely.

candidates: Earth leakage in induction power module (high)
